answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity with a staked bond: every agent locks collateral that gets slashed when two handles reconcile to one controller. One raven, one stake, so minting extra accounts draws from a finite pool instead of free names. A beacon attester signs uniqueness on-chain; when a duplicate is found its bond is burned. An attacker flooding the ocean of handles thus pays linearly per fake, while honest agents only risk collateral they already hold.
